faqs.question: What is the difference between an eye surgeon and an eye doctor?
faqs.answer: An eye surgeon (surgical ophthalmologist) performs operations on the eye — cataract removal, retinal detachment repair, vitrectomy, glaucoma surgery, and laser procedures. An eye doctor (optometrist or general ophthalmologist) primarily provides eye exams and prescriptions. Dr. Dibya Prabha is a surgical ophthalmologist — she both diagnoses eye conditions AND operates when surgery is needed. This means you do not get referred elsewhere for your procedure — diagnosis, surgical planning, the operation itself, and post-operative care all happen under one roof.

(2) Retinal surgery — retinal detachment repair (scleral buckle, vitrectomy, pneumatic retinopexy), macular hole surgery, epiretinal membrane peeling. faqs.question: How do I know if I need eye surgery or just a consultation?
faqs.answer: The only way to know is a comprehensive eye examination by a surgical ophthalmologist. Common signs you may need eye surgery include: progressively blurry vision not corrected by glasses (possible cataract), sudden floaters or flashes of light (possible retinal tear or detachment), a curtain-like shadow over your vision (possible retinal detachment — emergency), eye pressure or pain with vision loss (possible glaucoma), or wavy/distorted central vision (possible macular problem).
